headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon, outperforming top AI models with a 'significant leap' in cybersecurity
summary: Google's new Gemini 4 Carbon model leads benchmarks against GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5, but is currently exclusive to a select group of cybersecurity defense companies.
details: Google has officially launched Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier AI model, which is already outperforming top models from OpenAI and Anthropic on key benchmarks. The company highlights Carbon's top spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0), with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra trailing behind.

This new model offers significant gains in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity, building upon the earlier Argon model released this month. However, Gemini 4 Carbon is currently available only to a select group of cybersecurity defense companies.

Google plans to expand its availability to other partners within its Fairwind Program in the future. The company states that Carbon represents a "significant leap" in cyberdefense, enhancing its ability to find vulnerabilities and generate secure code.

Carbon holds the number one position on SEC-bench Pro, a benchmark for discovering real-world bugs, and ExploitGym, which measures a model's capacity to turn vulnerabilities into exploits. Google designed it for completing longer, complex tasks, with internal teams observing it run for days to tackle multi-step engineering challenges.

The model also demonstrates improved resistance to prompt injection attacks and better collaboration with users. Google claims Carbon offers greater "transparency and honesty," reducing "unsupported claims" by two times compared to its predecessor, Argon.
Gemini 4 Carbon will be introduced at the same competitive price as Argon: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
